landing.title: Less screen time. More city.
landing.description: Kaj ima? turns Zagreb’s open data into a public screen and ten minutes of the city on your device. No account, installation or ads.
landing.lead: Your tram. Tonight’s plans. What’s changing in your neighbourhood. Find what you need, then go on your way.
landing.intro: Kaj ima? brings the city’s open data to a public screen and into your hand.
landing.captureCaption: Actual application captures. Data in these images is not the current state.
landing.imageUnavailable: The image could not load. The description and all actions below are still available.

alt.kiosk: Public screen: Zagreb places on a map, culture, weather and neighbourhood information. The code is hidden in this example.
alt.phone: Phone after scanning: routes, events and city information arranged through the day.
alt.desktop: Desktop: local transport, weather and upcoming events, with direct access to every city information area.
alt.transport: Transport: ZET vehicle map, route and stop search, and route status.
alt.events: Events on a phone: dated listings with venue, category and source.
alt.peer: Another person’s phone in its own five-minute session.
alt.frozen: An expired session: a clearly labelled snapshot stays on the phone.

story.label: From a screen to an encounter
story.title: Come by. Find out. Move on.
story.intro: Access begins in a real place. And ends with more time for it.
story.approachBody: In a café, library or district office: a window onto what’s happening around you. The screen is useful even without a phone.
story.approachNote: A public screen. Useful on its own.
story.takeBody: Scan a code and the city is on your device for ten minutes. No account or installation. Browse privately, then use Screen to show something you choose on the public display.
story.takeNote: Ten minutes for what you need.
story.shareBody: The person next to you scans your code and gets five minutes of their own. Your time stays the same. A small reason to meet.
story.shareNote: Five minutes for another person, once.
story.leaveBody: Ten minutes later, refreshing stops. What you’re reading remains as a labelled snapshot, with sources and export options. Nothing calls you back.
story.safety: Safety is always open, without a code or a time limit.

evidence.label: One city, different views
evidence.title: What does the city have to tell you?
evidence.intro: No hunting through municipal websites. Each view starts with what is useful to you.
evidence.transitBody: ZET vehicles, stop search and route status. A route’s delay is not an arrival prediction.
evidence.dayBody: Transport and changes in your neighbourhood beside what is coming up: events, announcements and City decisions, each with its own time and source.
evidence.eventsBody: The city’s programme with a date, a place and an original source. Save an event to your calendar.
evidence.domains: Now · Map · Weather · Safety · City · Events

landing.liveSources: These are source data, not screenshots. A timestamp beside a reading belongs to its source; availability checks are shown separately.

live.healthPartial: Some displayed sources are not current

trial.label: Try the working prototype
trial.title: Over to you.
trial.intro: No public screen nearby? Set one up in your browser to try it.
trial.screenBody: Press one button and the screen shows the whole city. A district and a stop are chosen later, in the screen’s own settings. If you’ve already set up a screen, your existing setup will open.
trial.phoneTitle: Then take the city with you.
trial.phoneBody: Keep the screen open and scan its code with your phone. On a single device, open code entry in a second tab.
trial.sameDevice: Enter a code in another tab
trial.validity: A temporary screen lasts 24 hours. Scanning opens a normal ten-minute session.
trial.noPhone: No phone? The screen still shows the city, and Safety is open to everyone.

purpose.label: A public service, on a human scale
purpose.title: For people who live the city.
purpose.presenceBody: Nobody pays anything, in money or attention. No ads, accounts or personal tracking within the product.
purpose.screensBody: A café. A library. A district office. The vision is a network of useful screens on devices these places already have.
purpose.openBody: Every view names its source. The code is open, and derived datasets are available to download under their respective terms.
purpose.proposal: A working prototype for an application to the City of Zagreb. A pilot in city venues is proposed through funding and partnership with the City.
